note: CrowdSec integrates Drupal with the CrowdSec security network. It is driven by one config object crowdsec.settings (log_level, env dev|prod, api_timeout, cti_api_key, signal_scenarios[], scenarios[], plugins.<id>.{enable,ban_duration,leak_speed,bucket_capacity}). Ban plugins are a crowdsec_scenario plugin type (dir src/Plugin/CrowdsecScenario, attribute Drupal\crowdsec\Attribute\Scenario, base ScenarioPluginBase, manager plugin.manager.crowdsec_scenario). Three ship in-box: flood (drupal/auth-bruteforce), core-ban (drupal/core-ban), whisper (drupal/4xx-scan, buffered default; only whisper uses leak_speed+bucket_capacity). Config UI: /admin/config/services/crowdsec (route crowdsec.settings, permission 'administer site configuration'). Drush: crowdsec:enroll|signal|collect|test:signal|test:ip. Events under Drupal\crowdsec\Event\CrowdSecEvents (crowdsec.ip.banned etc). This site has NO live CrowdSec API/agent, so all medium/hard cases are grounded purely in local crowdsec.settings config reads/writes (no upstream calls).

evals.prompt: The Drupal CrowdSec module ships three built-in ban plugins that detect bad behaviour locally. Name them and say briefly what each one detects.
evals.expected_output: flood (Flood control bans, scenario drupal/auth-bruteforce) — IPs hitting Drupal flood control such as failed logins; core-ban (Administrator bans, drupal/core-ban) — IPs manually banned via core Ban / Advanced Ban; whisper (4xx response bans, drupal/4xx-scan) — IPs causing many 4xx responses within a time window.

evals.prompt: How do I add a custom CrowdSec 'scenario' (ban) plugin in my own Drupal module? What plugin directory, attribute and base class are involved, and how do I emit a signal for an IP?
evals.expected_output: Create a class in my_module/src/Plugin/CrowdsecScenario/ annotated with the #[Scenario(id, scenario, label, description, buffer)] attribute (Drupal\crowdsec\Attribute\Scenario) extending ScenarioPluginBase. Emit signals via ScenarioPluginManager::getPlugin('id')->addSignal($ip, $status, $targetUser). Its settings are auto-added under crowdsec.settings plugins.<id>.

evals.prompt: Where is the CrowdSec module configured in the Drupal admin (route/path), and which Drush command forces it to download and enforce the subscribed CrowdSec blocklists?
evals.expected_output: Configure it at /admin/config/services/crowdsec (route crowdsec.settings, permission 'administer site configuration'). drush crowdsec:collect refreshes/downloads the subscribed blocklists (Client::refresh()); it also runs on cron.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the live CrowdSec configuration and report: which environment (dev or prod) is CrowdSec set to, and what is the ban duration (in seconds) configured for the 4xx response ban plugin?
evals.expected_output: In crowdsec.settings, env is 'prod' and plugins.whisper.ban_duration (the 4xx-scan / whisper plugin) is 7200 seconds.

evals.prompt: One of CrowdSec's built-in ban plugins has been turned off on this site. Inspect the live crowdsec.settings configuration and state which ban plugin is currently disabled.
evals.expected_output: The flood plugin is disabled: crowdsec.settings plugins.flood.enable is FALSE (the core-ban and whisper plugins remain enabled).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the CrowdSec 4xx response ban plugin (whisper) so its threshold (bucket_capacity) is 25, meaning 25 bad requests in the time window are needed to ban an IP. Apply the change to the live crowdsec.settings configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set crowdsec.settings -> plugins.whisper.bucket_capacity to 25 (via the 'Threshold' field on the 4xx response bans plugin in the CrowdSec settings form, or drush cset crowdsec.settings plugins.whisper.bucket_capacity 25).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, disable CrowdSec's flood-control ban plugin (the one that locally bans IPs triggering Drupal flood control) while leaving the other ban plugins enabled. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set crowdsec.settings -> plugins.flood.enable to FALSE (untick 'Enable' on the Flood control bans plugin in the CrowdSec settings form, or drush cset crowdsec.settings plugins.flood.enable 0).
